problem: Knowledge-graph-based object-goal navigators build scene graphs from discrete one-hot object vectors and vote counting, which are misaligned with the agent's visual observations and generalize poorly to unseen goal objects. RL decision losses alone cannot align the two modalities.
motivation: Object-goal navigation requires the agent to understand its surroundings, and scene priors from knowledge graphs help in unfamiliar environments. Continuous language-aligned representations from vision-language pre-training (CLIP) could let the graph and the visual features share one space, which would enable zero-shot navigation to unseen object categories.
key_idea: Build a hierarchical zone-level knowledge graph whose nodes are continuous CLIP text embeddings of detected objects, and align it with CLIP visual features so that a hierarchical policy (GCN sub-goal planner plus LSTM low-level controller) can navigate to unseen goals.
insight: Replacing CLIP with an ImageNet ResNet-50 and one-hot encoding lowers SR by about 2.3 and SPL by about 2.5 on average (Tab. III), so the gain comes from the vision-language alignment. The zero-shot gap is far larger: AKGVP (CI) reaches 69.51 SR vs 54.75 for L-sTDE and 44.14 for EmbCLIP (Tab. II), and EmbCLIP uses only the CLIP image encoder without the language encoder and graph. Component ablation shows f_img and f_obj are critical (removing either collapses SR to 9-17%), while the graph feature adds about +4 SR and the previous action about +3 SR.
method: Aligned Encoder: a frozen CLIP ResNet-50 with the final FC layer of the visual encoder removed gives a 7x7x2048 image feature f_img. The CLIP language encoder embeds object names into continuous 1024-d object features f_obj, replacing one-hot vectors.

Spatial Location Clustering: Faster R-CNN detects goal objects at every (x,z,yaw,pitch) in training rooms. Object features are averaged over views per location (Eq. 1), then K-Means clusters locations into M zones per room.

Knowledge graph construction: nodes are zones whose features are the cluster-center means of object embeddings (Eq. 2). Edges are the adjacent probability between zones (Eq. 3). Graphs of different rooms of the same scene type are matched with Kuhn-Munkres and merged by averaging.

Graph Adaptation: node features are updated online from first-person observations with a trainable weight λ (Eq. 4). The update is episode-specific, and each episode starts from the same initial graph.

High-level controller: the target zone is the zone most likely to contain the goal. The controller plans the path with maximum product of edge probabilities from the current zone to the target zone and picks a sub-goal zone. A GCN processes the graph and the sub-goal node feature gives f_gra (1024-d).
Low-level controller: an LSTM takes concat(f_img, f_obj, f_gra, previous-action one-hot) and outputs one of 6 actions, trained with A3C using reward +5 on success and -0.01 per step.
AKGVP-CI variant: adds the causal-inference debiasing of L-sTDE to remove prediction bias from the knowledge-graph prior.

setting.backbone: Frozen CLIP ResNet-50 encoders + Faster R-CNN detector + GCN + LSTM policy (trained with A3C)
setting.training_data: AI2-THOR, 20 training rooms (of 30 rooms in 4 scene types), 6M training episodes with random start and goal. Six goal objects (Bowl, DeskLamp, Laptop, LightSwitch, Plate, StoveBurner) are held out for zero-shot training. CLIP pre-trained weights (frozen) are used.
setting.observation: egocentric first-person RGB (detector outputs plus CLIP features)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveAhead 0.5 m, RotateLeft/Right 45°, LookUp/Down 30°, Done
setting.privileged: Graph built from exhaustive exploration of training rooms with detector outputs at all positions; no privileged info at test time apart from that prior

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 test rooms, all goal objects (general navigation)
numbers.extra: includes L-sTDE causal inference; triplicate runs, mean±std; success radius 1.5 m

numbers_note: AI2-THOR is not in the canonical benchmark list, so it is labelled other:. Split is 20/5/5 rooms train/val/test.
results: AKGVP (CI) reaches 76.78 SR and 0.35 m DTS on AI2-THOR, beating L-sTDE (74.19 SR, 0.43 DTS). AKGVP (Base) has the best SPL (40.66). In zero-shot navigation to unseen objects, AKGVP (CI) gets 69.51 SR and 28.86 SPL, well above L-sTDE (54.75 / 16.64) and EmbCLIP (44.14 / 15.76).
limitations: Evaluated only in AI2-THOR with 22 object categories and a small room-level split, and there is no real-robot or large-scale benchmark such as HM3D or MP3D.

The graph is built from exhaustive exploration of the training rooms with a Faster R-CNN detector, and it relies on a fixed number of zones per room type. Unseen goals still need to be text-embeddable and detectable.
SPL of the CI variant is lower than the base one, and the paper offers only a speculative explanation.
